cases.message: unknown struct-query field on line "project title"

signature concept "supportLead" does not resolve: `use crm.concepts.{ supportLead }` imports it, and namespace crm declares no concept "supportLead" -- no mounted domain declares a concept "supportLead": declare it in crm, or correct the name
cases.note: memql#5433. The import is the authorization for a foreign signature concept, and one that supplies nothing used to bind the query to an EMPTY concept: with no filter it loaded and matched nothing.

cases.message: signature concept "salesLead" does not resolve: `use crm.concepts.{ salesLead }` imports it
cases.note: memql#5433. With a filter the empty binding was refused as `concept==""` does not lower, which named neither the concept nor the import.

cases.message: signature concept "supportNote" does not resolve: it is neither imported nor a same-domain concept
cases.note: The unimported half of the same rule, refused before memql#5433 and carrying its code since.

cases.message: `sort` is written twice -- `sort "row.createdAt", "desc"`, then `sort "title", "asc"` -- and a query takes one sort clause
cases.note: memql#5429. The body is read into one slot per clause, so the second sort line replaced the first one's keys without a word.
The same defect on the clause where it costs most: the second filter line replaced the first, and with it the ownership test.

cases.message: the name is taken by `use crm.shapes.{ supportTask }`, which imports a shape, not a concept -- alias it -- `use crm.shapes.{ supportTask as <another name> }` -- so "supportTask" names the concept
cases.note: memql#5433. The first import naming a name is the one resolution reads, so a shape import sharing the concept's name is aliased, not joined by a second import.
